transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-07-12 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 47 minutes (approx)
- Attendees: Alicia Gomez (Redwood AE), Samir Rao (Redwood SE), Evelyn Moore (Ridgeview VP Product), Dr. Sanjay Patel (Head of MLOps), Claire Liu (Security/Compliance), Marcus Reed (Cloud Infra)

Summary:
Quick renewal check-in to align on Ridgeview's upcoming contract renewal, discuss capacity uplift for the next 12 months, evaluate private on-prem pilot vs dedicated reserved capacity, and confirm security/compliance checklist for a HIPAA environment. Customer wants clear cost/latency tradeoffs and a short pilot before committing.

Topics:
- Current usage and forecasted uplift
- Regional expansion (EU + APAC) and latency zones
- Private on-prem pilot (air-gapped option) and VPC/KMS requirements
- Pricing & contract timing
- Benchmarks and test plan

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alicia Gomez: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, this is Alicia from Redwood, i'll hand off to Samir in a minute to go over the se side but first can i quickly confirm timeline? i think your renewal window is late july, Evelyn?
[00:12] Evelyn Moore: yeah that's right, renewal hits end of month, we're looking to lock something by, by the 31st if possible. internal procurement needs numbers this week ideally.
[00:22] Samir Rao: cool, i'll keep the technical part tight - quick note on attendees, who's driving the onprem pilot?
[00:28] Dr. Sanjay Patel: that's me, we're keen to try a private, on-prem image because of PHI handling. we've done some proofs with other vendors but latency and kv-cache behavior were different so i'm a bit cautious.
[00:40] Claire Liu: from security side we need SOC2, also encryption at rest, KMS with BYOK or HSM support, and audit logs - basically enterprise-grade telemetry.
[00:50] Alicia Gomez: totally understood. to be clear we can do two paths: option A is dedicated reserved capacity in our hosted infra with VPC peering and stricter data retention, option B is private on-prem / VPC private control plane where you manage keys. both have tradeoffs on cost and ops.
[01:07] Marcus Reed: can you remind us differences on latency SLOs? onprem should be lowest but we need to see numbers.
[01:13] Samir Rao: for hosted dedicated we usually guarantee p50 p99 targets per the SLA, but network hops can add a few ms. on-prem avoids that, and you'll also be able to run quantized variants which reduce cost but might slightly change quality. we'll run a KV-cache warmup test during the pilot to match your inference patterns.
[01:33] Evelyn Moore: our primary driver is predictable monthly cost and no surprises on token spikes - also data residency in eu is required for a subset of workloads. we might need an eu staging cluster.
[01:44] Alicia Gomez: makes sense - we can stage an EU geocluster and route certain routes there; that's part of the regional uplift plan.
[01:50] Dr. Sanjay Patel: one concern - if we go hosted dedicated and later need to move to private on-prem, how smooth is model rollover? PK caches and model versions have caused us headaches switching vendors.
[02:02] Samir Rao: good question - we've got a deployment abstraction so you can pin model versions independent of infra; in practice there are ops steps (kernel selection, quantization artifacts) but we provide migration scripts and a QA runbook. it's not instant but we've done successful rollovers with customers. sometimes prompts need slight retuning after quant changes.
[02:22] Claire Liu: also want to confirm logging retention and who has access - we can't have raw PHI in third-party logs.
[02:30] Alicia Gomez: absolutely. for private on-prem you control the logs. for dedicated hosted we offer filtered telemetry and can redact tokens; we also support customer-managed KMS for key wrapping. i'll include a redacted-telemetry options sheet.
[02:44] Marcus Reed: what about benchmarking? we need a throughput test and a latency profile for our most common endpoints.
[02:50] Samir Rao: we'll do a 48-hour stress run - two passes: one simulating typical dialogue lengths and one for peak short prompts. we'll capture p50/p90/p99 and cost per token. note that batching behavior will affect latency and unit cost; we'll show both tight-latency and batched-throughput configs.
[03:10] Evelyn Moore: and pricing - we need a committed capacity number and a burst plan, otherwise procurement won't sign.
[03:17] Alicia Gomez: understood. we'll present two pricing tiers: committed reserved (monthly/annual) with lower unit cost and a private pilot + migration uplift fee for on-prem.
[03:26] Dr. Sanjay Patel: one more technical: do you support HSM-backed KMS and an audit trail that's tamper-evident?
[03:33] Samir Rao: yes, we integrate with most cloud KMS and can do HSM-backed keys for the private control plane. audit trail is available — note sometimes event names are normalized in transcripts and the product name might be slightly off in the logs, but the raw event stream is intact.
[03:50] Claire Liu: can you send a sample of the compliance pack? SOC2 cert, penetration test summary, and a template for the DPIA?
[03:58] Alicia Gomez: yes i'll attach those.
[04:01] Marcus Reed: connectivity - our infra uses an MPLS-backed VPN to a colo, can you run the pilot there or do you need a container image?
[04:09] Samir Rao: we can do both - for air-gapped we ship an on-prem appliance image or helm charts depending on your environment. for VPN we may need a small egress path for metrics; if that's unacceptable we'll do an offline run and then a secure bundle transfer.
[04:26] Evelyn Moore: timeline check: pilot in July, then decision early August?
[04:30] Alicia Gomez: that's aligned to our scheduling. if procurement wants formal quote we need to get it to you by the 15th.
[04:36] Dr. Sanjay Patel: ok, sounds good. is there any differential in model behavior when you enable quantization? we saw hallucination uptick with some vendors.
[04:46] Samir Rao: quantization can slightly change logits; for most classification and generation flows we tune the temperature and do a small eval pass. part of our Optimize tooling recommends quant profiles per workload so we run regression on your prompt set. we'll include an eval run with the pilot.
[05:03] Claire Liu: legal wants to see indemnities language and data handling in the addendum. procurement will loop legal in after we see the numbers.
[05:12] Alicia Gomez: we'll add a redline-ready contract and the standard addendum.
[05:16] Marcus Reed: anything else from the team?
[05:19] Evelyn Moore: just to reiterate — key success metrics: p99 < 400ms for short prompts, throughput >= 120 requests/sec for batched flows, and no PHI in third-party logs.
[05:31] Alicia Gomez: noted. we'll include concrete bench numbers and confirm the on-prem plan meets the p99 target.

[05:38] Wrap and next steps
[05:38] Alicia Gomez: recap: Redwood to send pricing and compliance pack by 2027-07-15; Samir to kick off the private on-prem 48h baseline and share results by 2027-07-20; Ridgeview to send infra diagram + procurement slot for exec review. any objections?
[05:53] Evelyn Moore: no objections, sounds actionable.
[05:55] Dr. Sanjay Patel: fine from our side.
[05:57] Claire Liu: we'll follow up with a list of docs we need.
[06:00] Alicia Gomez: great, thanks everyone - we'll follow up via email with links to the SOC2 and the pilot-run checklist.

[06:06] Meeting end.
